To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
US is useful in 75% of cases, but is misleading/potentially harming in 13% of cases.

(1) US was useful in the majority of patients undergoing hand and wrist US in a district general trust; (2) US can be misleading and potentially harmful in some patients undergoing hand and/or wrist US, particularly in patients with carpal tunnel syndrome and tendinopathies; (3) US is useful in the majority, but misleading in a significant proportion of patients undergoing hand or wrist US, and therefore the usefulness of hand/wrist US needs to be carefully considered in each patient; (
high resolution US is useful in the majority of cases but misleading in a significant proportion, particularly in cases where US findings may lead to surgery or not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of musculoskeletal US in a busy district general hospital trust.
the usefulness of high resolution ultrasonography (HRS) of the hand and/or wrist.
the use of US of the hand/wrists, and the potential pitfalls and limitations of this imaging modality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, despite the fact that US is a valuable and important diagnostic tool for the hand and wrist surgeon, there are still a number of areas where it is potentially harmful and/or misleading.
, in the authors’ experience, US of the hand/wrists is a very useful investigation, but that it is not without its limitations.
, although US can be a useful investigation in the hand/wrist, it is not without pitfalls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

US is a useful investigation in the majority of cases, but there is a significant risk of misleading or harmful findings in some sub-groups, which could be reduced by mandatory training in musculoskeletal US.
US is a useful tool in the Hand and Upper Limb, but its misuse is a real risk and must be addressed.
US is useful for the hand and wrist in the majority of cases but is misleading in a significant minority.
